title: Meghan Markle Shares Rare Photos of Archie and Lilibet at Princess Diana's Estate
excerpt: The Duchess of Sussex posted a carousel of 11 family photos from a European summer holiday spanning Portugal and Britain, including a poignant visit to Althorp, where Diana is buried.
body:
• Meghan Markle posted 11 photos on Instagram captioned "Summer Holiday," offering rare glimpses of Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, during the family's European trip.
  • The carousel includes images from Althorp, Princess Diana's childhood home and burial site, showing Harry and Archie carrying flowers on the estate grounds.
  • The Sussex family also reunited with King Charles and Queen Camilla at Highgrove House — the first time the monarch had seen his grandchildren in more than four years.

A Carefully Curated Family Album

Meghan Markle shared a rare window into her family's private world on Thursday, posting 11 photographs on Instagram that chronicle a summer holiday through Portugal and the United Kingdom with Prince Harry, 41, and their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5.

https://x.com/ELLEmagazine/status/2080420291507892703

Captioned simply "Summer Holiday ☀️," the carousel captures the family on beaches, at dinner, and in one standout shot, seven-year-old Archie sitting in the cockpit of a plane wearing a captain's hat and reaching for the controls. Another image shows Harry playfully tossing Lilibet into the air over a swimming pool as Archie floats behind them, according to People.

The photos mark one of the most extensive public glimpses of the Sussex children in years. The family has largely shielded Archie and Lilibet from public view since relocating to Montecito, California, in 2020, making each new image a closely watched event in royal coverage.

A Walk Through Diana's Grounds

The most emotionally charged image in the set shows Harry, Archie, and Lilibet walking along a grassy path at Althorp, the Spencer family's ancestral estate in Northamptonshire where Princess Diana grew up and is buried. Father and son are both carrying bouquets of flowers, with Lilibet trailing behind in a floral dress and metallic sandals, clutching a small purse.

"At its heart it is just a family — and this family has gone through extraordinary upheavals. Whatever you think of the monarchy, this is a moment most of us wanted to see happen."

— Catherine Mayer, Royal Author, speaking to People

Diana is buried on a secluded island in the center of Althorp's Oval Lake, a location her brother Charles Spencer has described as deliberately remote to protect her resting place. The estate's website showed it was closed to visitors on July 10 and 11, aligning with the timing of the Sussex family's stay, according to Page Six. During their visit, the Sussexes stayed as guests of Charles Spencer at the 13,000-acre estate.

Harry previously wrote about bringing Meghan to visit his mother's grave for the first time in 2022. "At long last, I was bringing the girl of my dreams home to meet mum," he recounted in his 2023 memoir, Spare. The latest photos suggest Archie and Lilibet may now have visited their grandmother's burial site for the first time.

Portugal, Highgrove, and a Royal Reunion

Before heading to Britain, the family vacationed in Melides, a coastal town in Portugal's Alentejo region sometimes called the "Hamptons of Portugal." One photo in the carousel shows the exterior of a beachside restaurant, O Melidense, effectively pinpointing their holiday location. People reported in 2024 that the Sussexes had purchased a home in Portugal, near Princess Eugenie and her husband Jack Brooksbank.

The UK leg of the trip included a reunion with King Charles and Queen Camilla at Highgrove House, the monarch's private residence in Gloucestershire. According to People, it was only the third meeting between Harry and Charles since the King's 2024 cancer diagnosis and the first time Charles had seen his grandchildren in more than four years.

Harry had traveled to Britain earlier in July for charity events, including the one-year countdown celebration for the 2027 Invictus Games in Birmingham. A public dispute between the prince and the palace over security arrangements cast doubt on whether Meghan and the children would join him. Meghan ultimately arrived with the children on July 10 but made no public appearances during the trip, according to The Sun.

Fashion, Family, and Calculated Warmth

Style watchers noted that Meghan's black backless one-piece swimsuit, visible in a beach photo, echoed Princess Diana's well-known preference for similar silhouettes. Diana famously wore backless one-pieces during holidays in Nevis in 1993 and Saint-Tropez in 1997, InStyle reported. The carousel also includes a black-and-white portrait of Harry and Meghan laughing together, and a shot of the family's rescue beagle, Mamma Mia, sunbathing alongside Meghan.

The carefully assembled post arrives as the Sussexes continue to navigate a complex public narrative. Harry's UK visit was shadowed by a lost media trial, reported at £50 million, while tabloid reports have pointed to tensions over the couple's approach to royal reconciliation. By sharing moments of uncomplicated family warmth — children running into the ocean, a father and daughter at the pool — the post offers a deliberate counterpoint.

What's Next

The Highgrove reunion could signal a thaw in the strained relationship between Harry and the royal family. Whether this translates into more frequent visits to Britain or a more visible public role for Meghan during future trips remains to be seen. Harry's Invictus Games commitments will bring him back to the UK in 2027, and observers will be watching whether the family dynamic on display in these photos carries forward beyond the summer.
